text:
tyler: deploybot just rejected a staging push for rwd-service:staging-2026-03-21 citing a provenance attestation mismatch. anyone own that build?

deploybot: push rejected for rwd-service:staging-2026-03-21 - reason: provenance-attestation mismatch (manifest_sha != attested_origin_sha). run /deploybot inspect sha256:abc123... for details.

maria-sre: taking a look now.

tyler: i triggered the CI earlier (BUILD_ID=2026-03-21-17). CI logs show cosign sign/upload succeeded. snippet from CI logs:
```
cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY rwd-service@sha256:abc123...
cosign upload-attestation rwd-service@sha256:abc123... -> ok
ecr push rwd-service:staging-2026-03-21 -> failed: provenance mismatch
```

jenna: could be a mirror having rewritten layers or a stale tag retagged somewhere. is digest in ECR different?

alex.dev: i just queried GCR and ECR. same tag exists in both but digests differ. CI produced sha256:abc123..., ECR shows sha256:def456...

release-manager: change window ends in ~45m. we should avoid promoting any canary->prod. proposals: 1) pin canary to last-good digest and promote, 2) rebuild and re-sign, or 3) manual override.

maria-sre: we should avoid overrides. we have two safe moves: retag last-good digest (if attestation exists) or re-sign known-good digest. deploybot enforces attestation for promotions.

tyler: quick verification command I ran:
```bash
aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name rwd-service --image-ids imageTag=staging-2026-03-21 --query 'images[0].imageId.imageDigest'
# returns: sha256:def456...
```
CI artifact: sha256:abc123 -> mismatch confirmed.

alex.dev: suggestion: mark current tag quarantined, pin canary to last-good digest sha256:xyz789, attach cosign attestation for xyz789, then allow promotion. i'll handle attestation if infra ok with it.

tyler: can you retag last-good to staging-canary? I'll attempt a manual retag now: 
```bash
# fetch manifest for known-good
aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name rwd-service --image-ids imageDigest=sha256:xyz789 --query 'images[0].imageManifest' --output text > manifest.json
aws ecr put-image --repository-name rwd-service --image-tag staging-canary --image-manifest file://manifest.json
```

deploybot: detected manual retag 'staging-canary' -> digest sha256:xyz789. promotion blocked: missing cosign attestation for rwd-service@sha256:xyz789.

maria-sre: we need an attestation present. no bypass. alex.dev, can you attach the attestation for xyz789?

alex.dev: on it. steps i'll run locally:
```bash
cosign attach attestation --key $COSIGN_KEY --predicate predicate.json rwd-service@sha256:xyz789
# then push to registry
```
I'll update here when done.

jenna: i'll open a quick incident ticket to track: INFRA-XXXX, include build ids, digests, and timeline.

tyler: also update the release notes / change log: note that canary is pinned while we investigate.

alex.dev: cosign attach succeeded and attestation present (attestation id: att-2026-03-21-1705). deploybot: please re-evaluate.

deploybot: attestation discovered for rwd-service@sha256:xyz789. Promotion now permitted. To proceed run: `/deploy promote staging-canary -> canary`.

tyler: /deploy promote staging-canary -> canary

deploybot: promotion started. rolling canary to 5% (instances: 12 -> 1). monitoring metrics.

release-manager: :thumbsup: good work. keep the quarantined tag (staging-2026-03-21) marked and add note to release notes that a rebuild/resign is scheduled tonight.

maria-sre: assigning follow-up to infra team to root cause why digest changed between registries. ticket INFRA-XXXX updated.

jenna: adding a small postmortem checklist: 1) verify mirror pipeline integrity, 2) verify cosign upload path, 3) add a guard that disallows silent retags for release tags.

tyler: thanks all. will monitor canary and update if anything flaps.
